issue.title: The 10 best American sitcoms of all time

caption: Season 18 of It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia drops this week, making it the longest-running live-action sitcom in American TV history. To celebrate, we picked the show plus books about terrible people and the movies that got Philly right. From Today's Pix.
altText: Headline reads: The 10 best American sitcoms of all time. Subhead reads: It's Always Sunny turns 18. Here's what to watch, read, and skip.

Pull quote reads: Charlie, Dennis, Mac, Dee, and Frank are awful people who have spent two decades running the worst bar in Philadelphia. Attribution: Pix editors, on It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia.

Body text explains Season 18 of It's Always Sunny drops this week as the longest-running live-action sitcom in American TV history, celebrating with picks of shows, books about terrible people, and movies that got Philadelphia right.
TLDR list: Watch: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia — Season 18 starts now. Read: Filth — narrated partly by a tapeworm inside a cop. Watch: Rocky — the Art Museum steps became a pilgrimage site.
Featured recommendation: It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia by FXX. Worth watching because two decades in, the worst people in Philly are still finding new ways to fail. Recommended by Pix editors.

Stat: 18 seasons of the longest-running live-action sitcom in American TV history. Moment: Rob McElhenney, Glenn Howerton, and Charlie Day created the show as a $200 proof-of-concept in 2005. Call to action: Read the full list in Today's Pix.
